extraction.name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset for object recognition, segmentation, and scene understanding. It contains images of complex everyday scenes with common objects in their natural context. The dataset includes 91 object types and 2.5 million labeled instances in 328,000 images, with per-instance segmentations to aid in precise object localization.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected by querying for pairs of object categories, or pairs of object and scene categories, to find non-iconic images with contextual relationships. At most 5 photos taken by a single photographer within a short time window were downloaded. In rare cases, single categories were searched and explicitly filtered to remove iconic images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Flickr (photos uploaded by amateur photographers with searchable metadata and keywords)
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Near-duplicate images existing across splits were explicitly removed using a detection algorithm, and images were grouped by photographer and date taken to minimize the chance of near-duplicates.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation pipeline consisted of three primary tasks: (a) category labeling using a hierarchical approach to determine which objects are present, (b) instance spotting by placing a cross on top of each instance, and (c) instance segmentation. A verification step was also performed where multiple workers judged each segmentation for quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) and a modified user interface from the OpenSurfaces project
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Worker precision and recall were analyzed by comparing to dedicated expert workers. The union of 8 AMT workers achieved greater recall than any expert worker. Disagreement analysis showed that even dedicated experts often disagree on object presence due to inherent ambiguity in the image or category definitions.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 8 workers for category labeling and instance spotting per image; 1 worker for instance segmentation; 3 to 5 workers for segmentation verification.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset was split into two roughly equal parts for a faster release schedule (2014 release and a cumulative 2015 release). The dataset will evolve and grow over time, with up-to-date information available online.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently only labels 'things' (objects with clear boundaries) and not 'stuff' (materials/objects with no clear boundaries like sky or street). For images containing more than 10-15 instances of a category, individual instances are not distinguished and are instead marked as 'crowds' using a single segment.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing for object classification, object detection, and instance segmentation. Annotations for train and validation data are released, but test set annotations are withheld for automatic evaluation on an evaluation server.
